rows.n: edge deployment
rows.b: Running the model on the device at the network's edge — phones, laptops, gadgets — instead of a data center.

rows.n: Elo rating
rows.b: A chess-style skill score from head-to-head model comparisons, as used on public leaderboards.

rows.n: embedding
rows.b: A list of numbers that captures a word's meaning, learned so that similar words end up with similar numbers.

rows.n: embedding matrix
rows.b: The big lookup table mapping every token ID to its learned embedding vector.

rows.n: emergent ability
rows.b: A skill that appears suddenly once a model gets big enough, absent in smaller versions.

rows.n: encoder
rows.b: The transformer half that reads a whole input at once, building a rich understanding before anything is generated.

rows.n: encoder-decoder model
rows.b: A model with both halves: the encoder reads the input, the decoder writes the output, as in translation systems.

rows.n: endpoint
rows.b: The web address a model listens on for incoming requests.

rows.n: EOS token
rows.b: The special end-of-sequence token whose appearance tells generation to stop.

rows.n: epoch
rows.b: One full pass through the entire training dataset.

rows.n: eval bias
rows.b: Ways a test can mislead — leaked data, judge favoritism, or questions that reward the wrong thing.

rows.n: eval harness
rows.b: The software framework that runs benchmarks consistently so scores are comparable.

rows.n: evaluation
rows.b: Measuring how good a model actually is, with tests rather than vibes.

rows.n: exact match
rows.b: A strict score that only counts answers identical to the expected one.

rows.n: expert
rows.b: One specialist feed-forward network inside a mixture-of-experts layer, typically good at certain topics or patterns.
